info.bio:
Kansas es una banda norteamericana fundada en 1970, su estilo destacó en el Rock Progresivo. Sus integrantes originales son: Dave Hope (bajo), Phil Ehart (batería), Robby Steinhardt (violín), Steve Walsh (teclado y voz), Rich Williams (guitarra). Anteriormente formaron la banda White Clover, en su ciudad natal de Topeka, Kansas. Después de la llegada de Kerry Livgren (guitarra y teclado) el nombre fue cambiado por Kansas.
En 1983, algunos de los integrantes han ido cambiando.

scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El «sonido» por encima de la melodía, el ritmo y la armonía: Electric Light Orchestra inventa el «high-tech pop»; Supertramp, Alan Parsons Project, Kansas, Styx y Split Enz. El valor de la producción define a Steely Dan (el pop-jazz pulido de los yuppies), Hall & Oates, los Fleetwood Mac de Rumours y Tusk, Toto, el «muro de sonido» titánico de Jim Steinman (Bat Out Of Hell) y la Penguin Cafe Orchestra. A finales de los setenta, el art-rock culmina en los supergrupos: 10cc, Godley & Creme, Foreigner, UK, Asia, Sky.

podcast.title: Clergy Rejection of "Dust in the Wind"
podcast.body: Some clergy members expressed rejection of the message in "Dust in the Wind" because of the line "all we are is dust in the wind," illustrating the risks involved in recording songs with potentially controversial religious or philosophical themes. "some members of the clergy rejected this song's message, because of the line all we are is dust in the wind."

podcast.title: Comparison to Emerson, Lake & Palmer
podcast.body: Kansas was often compared to Emerson, Lake & Palmer, with suggestions that Kerry Livgren's lyrics in "Dust in the Wind" might have borrowed themes or lines, such as from ELP's "Carnival 9." "Livgren was borrowing from Emerson Lake and Palmer, a band that Kansas was often compared to, with the line from Carnival 9."

podcast.title: Near-Drop from Record Label
podcast.body: In 1975, Don Kirshner was on the verge of dropping Kansas from his record label due to their lack of a hit single, despite acceptable album sales. The band was saved by the success of "Carry On Wayward Son" from their album *Leftoverture*. "Don Kirschner... was just about to drop Kansas from his record label in 1975."

xref.title: Lou Reed's Departure and Classic Lineup Breakup (1970)
xref.body: The classic lineup of The Velvet Underground was shattered when Lou Reed left the group after a performance consisting of two sets at Max's Kansas City in New York on August 23, 1970, marking an abrupt end to their initial phase. "The classic lineup was shattered after Lou left the group after a performance in New York on August 23rd 1970."

xref.title: Alleged Kidnapping Plot Against Wichita Mayor
xref.body: Meredith Douty, a musician from Wichita, Kansas, performing under the name Kat Head, was allegedly involved in a plan to kidnap and slit the throat of the city's mayor. Douty's motivation stemmed from his strong opposition to the mask mandates declared by the mayor, but the FBI intervened before the plan could be carried out. "He was so upset about masked mandates in the city that he allegedly planned to kidnap and slashed the throat of the mayor who declared that mandate."

xref.title: Early Adult Life in New York
xref.body: At seventeen, Nancy moved to New York City where she worked as a stripper and occasionally as a prostitute to earn extra money. She became involved in the punk scene, frequenting clubs like CBGB and Max's Kansas City, sometimes carrying drugs for bands. "She moved to New York, where she worked for a while as a stripper, and when she needed extra money, she turned tricks. She was just 17."

xref.title: Early Struggles and Financial Support
xref.body: In the late 90s, the New York rock scene was considered dead, with few venues beyond private parties in Brooklyn warehouses. The Strokes worked through these challenges with Albert Hammond Jr.'s father's credit card and part-time jobs. Julian Casablancas was a bartender at Max's Kansas City, Nikolai Fraiture worked at a video store, Fabrizio Moretti made smoothies, and Albert Hammond Jr. worked at Kim's video. "Along with Albert's dad's credit card, they also had part-time jobs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Layne Staley's Drug Addiction and Decline
xref.body: Around 1995, Layne Staley's drug habit spiraled out of control, leading to his virtual disappearance from 1996 onward. His last performance with the band was on July 3, 1996, in Kansas City, during a tour with KISS. He became a severe addict, barricading himself in his Seattle condo, where he painted, played video games, and had drugs delivered, leaving the band paralyzed. "Lane turned into an irreparable junkie, barricading himself in his Seattle condo where he painted, played video games, and had all his drugs delivered to the door."
